summary: Rounding to the nearest ten with "5 rounds up" is pure integer math: add 5, then chop off the last digit (T1 — direct formula). We avoid Python's `round()`, which uses a different rule.

blocks.title: Read N
blocks.text: We need a real number for the math, so `int()` it.

blocks.title: Add 5, then chop the last digit
blocks.text: Adding 5 pushes any last digit 5–9 over the next ten. `// 10` drops the last digit and `* 10` puts a zero back: 247 → 252 → 25 → 250, and 5 → 10 → 1 → 10. Python's `round(25, -1)` gives 20 (it rounds halves to the even side), so it would fail the `5` cases.

blocks.title: The same rule written the long way
blocks.text: These comments show the statement's version: look at `N % 10` (the last digit) and either go up to the next ten or down. Useful if you find the trick hard to trust in the contest.

pitfalls: Forgetting the final `* 10` and printing 25 instead of 250.
